# Etsy.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/etsy-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/etsy-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects product listing data from Etsy.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Etsy.com Product, Shop and Search Data](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-etsy-com-product-review-data)
- **Code:** [`etsy.py`](etsy.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Product pages](results/products.json) · [Shop pages](results/shops.json) · [Search pages](results/search.json)

## What it scrapes

- Etsy search pages for listing data
- Etsy product pages for product data
- Etsy shop pages for shop data

## Functions

- `scrape_search(url, max_pages=None)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape product listing data from Etsy search pages
- `scrape_product(urls)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape trustpilot company pages
- `scrape_shop(urls)` → `List[Dict]`

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import etsy


async def main():
    search = await etsy.scrape_search(url="https://www.etsy.com/search?q=wood+laptop+stand", max_pages=3)
    product = await etsy.scrape_product(
        urls=[
            "https://www.etsy.com/listing/1552627931",
            "https://www.etsy.com/listing/529765307",
        ],
    )
    shop = await etsy.scrape_shop(
        urls=[
            "https://www.etsy.com/shop/FalkelDesign",
            "https://www.etsy.com/shop/JoshuaHouseCrafts",
        ],
    )


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields of the sample output (top-level keys of the first item):

- [`results/products.json`](results/products.json): `@type`, `@context`, `url`, `name`, `sku`, `gtin`, `description`, `image`, `category`, `brand`, `logo`, `aggregateRating`, `offers`, `review`, `material`
- [`results/shops.json`](results/shops.json): `@context`, `@type`, `itemListElement`, `numberOfItems`, `url`
- [`results/search.json`](results/search.json): `productLink`, `productTitle`, `productImage`, `seller`, `listingType`, `productRate`, `numberOfReviews`, `freeShipping`, `productPrice`, `priceCurrency`, `originalPrice`, `discount`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`etsy.py`](etsy.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/etsy-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_product_scraping`, `test_shop_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
